summary: Cedarbridge Health: intermittent conversation timeouts triggering cascade failovers across regions — customer urgent escalation and post-incident action plan
description: Issue summary: During customer peak between 07:25–08:40 UTC on 2026-03-10, Cedarbridge experienced intermittent conversation timeouts (stream disconnects) that caused client-side retries and triggered automated failover policies. The failover amplified load on alternate regions and on Dedicated routing lanes, resulting in elevated tail latency, transient 5xx spikes, and a burst of duplicate completions. Impact: Multiple production customers within the Cedarbridge account saw degraded chat UX, missing streaming tokens, and a measurable billing delta from replayed requests. Environment: Cedarbridge private deployment (VPC peering) with private-controlplane in us-east and eu-west, serving-runtime running quantized and unquantized variants. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained streaming chat traffic with session affinity enabled and a mix of short/long prompts. 2) Simulate a TLS renegotiation on the control plane (internal test only). 3) Observe prefix/KV caching misses and client retries. Observed behavior: - Streaming response chains aborted intermittently at ~1–4s into response. - Clients retried and triggered fallback to alternate region/pinned model variant. - Serving runtime logged transient kernel-selection stalls (latency spikes) on quantized variant. - Control plane reported a brief spike in connection churn during TLS renegotiation window. Temporary mitigation applied: - Disabled aggressive retry policy for Cedarbridge customer at the API gateway (rate-limit + de-duplication). - Temporarily pinned traffic to primary region (us-east) for sessions originated in us-east. - Rolling restart of two serving-runtime pods in eu-west. Next steps: Complete root-cause analysis for TLS renegotiation impact on session affinity, implement server-side de-dup token, and provide customer credit for duplicate completions if billing delta confirmed.

resolution_summary: Workarounds: gateway-level retry suppression and temporary region pinning successfully stopped duplicate completions and stabilized tail latency. Root cause: interaction between control-plane TLS renegotiation (during certificate refresh) and session-affinity rebinding which caused KV/prefix cache misses and increased kernel-selection thrash on quantized variants. Permanent fix path: add session rebind backoff to control plane, increase resilience of prefix cache warmup, and implement server-side idempotency token for streaming responses.
postincident_actions: 1) Control plane: change TLS rotation to staggered, connection-safe rolling updates; owner: Network team; due: 2026-03-24.
2) Runtime: add a soft-warmup window to prefix/KV cache on rebind to avoid cold-path kernel thrash; owner: Runtime team; due: 2026-03-31.
3) API Gateway: permanent de-duplication middleware for streaming requests (idempotency token); owner: API team; due: 2026-04-07.
4) Billing: run deduplication heuristics and reconcile duplicate completions for Cedarbridge; owner: BillingOps; due: 2026-03-18.
5) Customer communication: send final incident report and compensation summary; owner: CS; due: 2026-03-15.
6) Runbook update: add checklist for TLS rotation impact on private-controlplane customers and test cases that simulate session rebind; owner: SRE; due: 2026-03-20.
7) Postmortem: 1-week follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-17 to validate mitigations and close actions.
notes_for_engineering: Reproduce in staging using the provided pcap and TLS-rotation script before landing changes to control plane.
Prioritize idempotency token experiment in the API gateway canary; measure any latency impact in isolation.
Telemetry: add a dedicated metric for 'session_rebind_count' per customer to catch early signs of similar regressions.
